_how_to_use: Copy this file, fill in every field, and run: python analyse.py cases/<your_file>.json. Keys starting with '_' are ignored. State in 'provenance' whether each value is published or assumed, and where it comes from.
name: my_site
description: One sentence: what the site produces and what the stream loads represent.
reference: Full citation of the source of the stream data.
_stream_file_format: CSV columns: stream, type (hot/cold), T_in_C, T_out_C, dT_shift_K, and ONE of Q_<unit> (e.g. Q_kW, Q_kWh_per_t) or CP_<unit> (e.g. CP_kW_per_K). Latent loads: use a 1 K temperature interval.
_ambient_T_C: Ambient temperature [°C]. External (non-process) heat pump sources must be at or below it.

heat_pumps._eta_lorenz: Lorenz efficiency, 0 < eta <= 1. 0.55 is from Padullés et al. (2026); justify any other value.
heat_pumps._source_T_C: Default heat source temperature on the T* axis. Use the process cooling level below the pinch, or ambient.
heat_pumps._sink_levels: Candidate sinks, sized automatically from the GCC from lowest to highest. 'gcc_max' = isothermal sink at the highest GCC temperature. A level may set its own T_source_C.

_basis: Optional. {'type': 'power', 'operating_hours_per_year': h} for loads in kW/MW, or {'type': 'per_product', 'production_per_year': x, 'production_unit': 'hl'} for loads such as kWh/hl. Use null if unknown: no annual figures are then reported.

sources.prices: cite the price source, period, band and tax basis

_economics: Optional; needs 'basis'. Any key left out takes the default in pinch/economics.py (DEFAULTS, each with its source). For a 'power' basis, operating_hours_per_year must match the basis. heat_recovery_equipment: list of [kind, size] (kinds: hr_tank [m3], heat_pump/mvr/electric_boiler [kW]) to evaluate a site without heat recovery.
_screening: Optional plausibility thresholds; defaults and their sources are in pinch/design.py.
